root_cause.text: The regsafe() function failed to properly handle comparison of packet pointer ranges when one or both ranges were negative (BEYOND_PKT_END or AT_PKT_END), allowing it to incorrectly return true when comparing BEYOND_PKT_END with a valid packet range N, causing the verifier to skip exploration of valid program states.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit handling for negative range values (special cases for BEYOND_PKT_END and AT_PKT_END) by checking `if (rold->range < 0 || rcur->range < 0)` and requiring exact equality in these cases. The original code only checked `if (rold->range > rcur->range)`, which would not catch the case where rold->range == BEYOND_PKT_END (negative) and rcur->range == N (positive), allowing an unsafe return of true. The fix ensures that when either range is negative, the ranges must match exactly, preventing the false positive that would skip valid state exploration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix register state comparison to correctly handle negative range values representing packet boundary markers by requiring exact equality instead of applying the standard range comparison logic.
intent_record.what: Modified the range comparison logic in the regsafe function to add a special case handler for negative range values before the existing positive range comparison. When either rold->range or rcur->range is negative, the code now requires exact equality (rold->range == rcur->range); otherwise, it falls through to the original comparison logic for non-negative ranges.
intent_record.how: This change affects how the verifier determines if two register states are safely equivalent. Previously, any rold->range > rcur->range would fail the safety check. Now, negative ranges (which represent special packet boundary states like AT_PKT_END or BEYOND_PKT_END) are handled separately with stricter equality requirements, while non-negative ranges continue using the original relaxed comparison. This prevents false positives when comparing registers with special boundary markers.
